messages:

Subject: Post-call recap: capacity readiness & reserved GPU sizing for Skyline Analytics

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared list of constraints and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points
- Unpredictable inference cost and token spend across bursty product events (marketing-led launches).
- Tail latency spikes when several teams run generation jobs concurrently (multi-tenant interference).
- Need for strict data isolation and auditability for enterprise customers (SOC 2 scope).
- Difficulty guaranteeing throughput during peak windows while keeping unit cost reasonable.

Current stack (what you shared)
- K8s on GCP with Triton for model serving (internal ops team).
- Models: mix of quantized Llama2-70B for chat, a 30B in-house fine-tuned model for retrieval-augmented generation.
- Session style product that keeps KV caches warm for returning users; cold-cache latency matters.

Success criteria you called out
- Predictable sustained throughput: ~3k requests/sec typical, ability to burst to ~6k for short windows (~15–30 minutes).
- P95 latency target for interactive prompts: <= 300ms for short prompts (under 1k tokens).
- Data isolation per tenant and SOC 2 Type II evidence for logs/retention.
- Budget guardrails: target blended cost per 1k requests that’s demonstrably below current unit economics.

Preliminary Redwood Dedicated fit thoughts
- Reserved GPU pools to provide capacity isolation and predictable TPS (recommend starting with a mixed pool of A100-80GB equivalents + some L40x for cost-sensitive paths).
- Autoscaling policy: configured baseline reserved capacity to cover sustained 3k TPS, with a burst bucket to absorb short 6k spikes and automatic fallback to a slightly smaller but compatible model variant if needed.
- Workload optimizations we discussed: KV prefix caching, request coalescing for near-identical prompts, and async batching for non-interactive backfills.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the 3k sustained / 6k burst numbers and typical burst duration (15–30m)? Any seasonality to expect (daily vs weekly vs quarterly)?
2) Security attachments: please send any SOC2 questions or specific control IDs you need evidence for (I attached our SOC2 summary).
3) We'll run a short sizing exercise: Ben will draft a suggested reserved pool config and cost estimate.
4) Schedule a technical deep dive (recording + notes) next week to walk infra and autoscaling knobs.

Attachments sent: redwood-dedicated-pricing-q4-2026.xlsx (pricing & a few sample pool configs)

If that looks right I’ll kick off the sizing draft and get us a tentative tech-deep-dive slot.

Best,
Priyom Das

Thanks, Priyom — this is great and captures our needs. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Sustained vs burst: our baseline request rate is closer to 2.5k RPS during business hours, but we regularly see 10–12x increases for marketing pushes; those bursts are usually 10–20 minutes. We can provide a recent 30-day QPS chart.
- Model mix: the Llama2-70B is used for customer-facing chat; heavier internal analytics pipelines hit the 30B. We can tolerate a small degradation in quality for bursts (e.g., fall back to a 13B variant) as long as we keep session continuity.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is mandatory; we need log retention of 12 months and export hooks for audits.
- Procurement: target decision window is end of Q1 2027.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll share the QPS/export for the last 30 days and the internal security checklist.
- Please send any reference architecture for dedicated pools and typical pool sizes you’ve seen for similar customers.

Appreciate the clear next steps — Sarah
